paragraphs.text: Only 8 events are documented here, along with 55 people and places, and some locations in this account are approximate.
The jurist Ahmad ibn Hanbal was born here in 780 CE and the future caliph al-Ma'mun in 786 CE.
The siege of Baghdad, part of a civil war between al-Amin and al-Ma'mun for the Abbasid Caliphate, lasted from August 812 until September 813.
Al-Ma'mun reigned from 813 until 833 and promoted the flowering of learning and the sciences in Baghdad.
The traveller Ahmad ibn Fadlan was born here in 879 CE and the historian Al-Mas'udi around 896 CE.
A battle of Baghdad is recorded in 932 CE, with no further detail.
In 942 CE the Hamdanids defeated the Baridis near al-Mada'in in a four-day battle for control over Baghdad.
In 946 CE the Buyids under Mu'izz al-Dawla expelled the Hamdanids from Baghdad after months of fighting within the city.
Seljuk forces blockaded the Abbasid capital for fifty days in 1136 CE and besieged it again in 1157 CE, when Caliph al-Muqtafi successfully defended it.
In 1258 CE a Mongol army under Hulegu took and sacked Baghdad, and the caliph al-Musta'sim was killed alongside hundreds of thousands of his subjects.
A sédition de Karkh is also recorded in 1258 CE, with no further detail.
